Definition: from G4509; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked:--vile.
BiblicalUsage: A man with a gold ring in goodly apparel comes in, and there comes in also a poor man in vile raiment, and the assembly shows him to the worst seat. He which is filthy, let him be filthy still, says the close of the book.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the vile raiment is the test of the assembly, and the filthy at the last are those who chose to stay so.
RelatedPeople: James, Brother of Jesus; John the Apostle
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
